change.summary: Process targets can issue bounded HTTP requests against the supervised service, assert status/body text, retain the complete response before assertion failure, and attribute transport loss to authoritative process exit.

intermediateFinding.head: e4ca22b483f9d0608d7991f612612b341fd7a856
intermediateFinding.observed: A supervised service exit could surface fetch failed just before child close was observable.
intermediateFinding.correction: On HTTP transport failure, allow at most 25 ms for the already-authoritative terminal signal before classifying a generic network failure.

challengePass.question: Would a whole Hurl/Testcontainers/MockServer dependency or a new standalone API target outperform the narrow native process HTTP step now?
challengePass.reason: The native step proves the missing request/assert/evidence behavior with zero dependency and shares Ferrum process lifecycle, cancellation, identity and redaction. External candidates remain isolated until identical-workload evidence proves additional capability or measurable benefit.

nextExperiments: Compare a disposable Testcontainers Node HTTP/OpenAPI fixture with the same local process fixture for setup, cleanup, identity and evidence parity.
Run a fixed-seed bounded Schemathesis stateful workload and require a minimized repeatable seeded-defect reproducer.
Put the same fixture behind Toxiproxy and prove latency/reset/recovery with exact fault configuration.
Compare WuppieFuzz only after Schemathesis establishes the lightweight stateful baseline.
guardrails: No response/evidence truncation or item caps introduced.
No new dependency required for the HTTP capability.
Linux, Windows, browser matrix, MV3, Spaces, Workbench, Electron, packaged desktop, Selenium Grid, Lightpanda, Android/Appium and MCP gates remained green.
External fuzz/mock/container tools stay additive until real-runtime benefit is proven.
